sections.heading: Linear buyer question and thesis
sections.body:

Product/engineering teams wanting modern UX; Startups replacing Jira complexity; Issue-centric software delivery. Linear is a fast, opinionated issue tracker for software product teams (cycles, projects, roadmaps). Free covers limited issues/members; Basic/Standard ~list price–list price annua. That catalogue mix is the Linear setup filter — not a generic project-management lecture.

Buyer question: for task boards teams, is Linear worth the Basic unlock, or does Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS kill the rollout?

ROI gate: Linear is worth the Basic spend if task boards + timeline / Gantt are weekly; not worth buying when Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS.

Best for: Product/engineering teams wanting modern UX; Startups replacing Jira complexity; Issue-centric software delivery (Product/engineering teams wanting modern UX).

Poor fit when: Marketing Work OS buyers; Spreadsheet PMO buyers; Non-technical company-wide rollout. Avoid if Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS would block go-live.

sections.heading: Linear limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS; Leaner automation than Jira Enterprise; Limited non-eng collaboration surfaces because it forces process changes or add-ons around Linear when task boards is the job.

Pricing interpretation: stay on Free until task boards is mandatory; plan jumps to Basic only after that hinge is proven.

Plan trade-off: you gain task boards at the expense of Seat minimums and AI credit bundles vs published per-seat floors — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Free · free · task boards | Basic | Business.

Alternative context: unlike Jira, Linear is preferable when Product/engineering teams wanting modern UX because task boards plus task boards match; prefer Jira when Marketing Work OS buyers because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Linear
sections.body:
Workflow advantage: Linear is faster for task boards when task boards; timeline / Gantt; workload and resources; automations and workflows is in-product; skip when Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS because that loop lives elsewhere.

Implementation complexity: setup requires confirming task boards ownership and Zapier before rollout — do not scale seats first.

Conclusion: Linear is worth it if Product/engineering teams wanting modern UX and task boards are weekly; skip Linear if Marketing Work OS buyers. That is the decision, not a template with the logo swapped.
